long_video.title: How Noise-Cancelling Headphones Work (Sound That Erases Sound)
long_video.description:
Noise-cancelling headphones do not just block sound, they fight it with more sound. In this video we see how microphones and a flipped anti-noise wave cancel engine hum, why it works far better on low steady sounds than on voices, how padding handles the rest, and how a frustrated engineer on a flight helped start it all.

Chapters
00:00 Intro: silence made from sound
00:43 Push and pull at the same time
01:26 Peaks, troughs and hertz
02:10 Microphone, chip, speaker
02:51 Feedforward, feedback, hybrid
03:31 Why low sounds are easier
04:16 What it can and can't cancel
05:00 Passive isolation does the rest
05:40 From a patent to a plane seat
06:24 Transparency and adaptive modes
07:05 Recap in three points
07:33 Your turn

Key facts (checked November 2026):
- ANC uses a microphone and an out-of-phase wave to cancel noise by destructive interference; works best on constant low-frequency sound, less on voices and sudden sounds; high frequencies are handled by passive isolation (Wikipedia: Noise-cancelling headphones)
- Feedforward (outside mic), feedback (inside mic) and hybrid designs (Wikipedia)
- History: Paul Lueg patent 1936; Amar Bose's idea on a flight in 1978; Rutan and Yeager wore prototype Bose headsets on the 1986 non-stop round-the-world flight; Bose consumer QuietComfort from 2000 (Wikipedia)
- Some people feel dizziness with strong ANC; lowering ANC strength can help (SoundGuys)
- Wavelengths calculated with the speed of sound at about 343 m/s

Sources
- Noise-cancelling headphones (Wikipedia): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noise-cancelling_headphones
- How do noise-cancelling headphones work (SoundGuys): https://www.soundguys.com/how-do-noise-cancelling-headphones-work-12380
